name: Insider Threat: Excessive Failed Logons (Brute Force / Password Spray)
description: Fires when a single account accumulates 8 or more failed logons (Windows event 4625) within 5 minutes - classic brute-force or password-spray behaviour.

name: Insider Threat: Account Lockout
description: A user account was locked out (Windows event 4740), often the tail end of a brute-force attempt or credential misuse.

name: Insider Threat: User Added to Privileged Group
description: A user was added to a security-enabled group (Windows events 4728/4732/4756). Watch for additions to Domain Admins / Administrators - a common privilege-escalation and persistence step. Requires the AD Domain Controller to be logging.

name: Insider Threat: New User Account Created
description: A new user account was created (Windows event 4720). In a small AD, account creation is rare and worth review - rogue-account creation is a persistence technique. Requires the AD Domain Controller to be logging.

name: Defense Evasion: Windows Security Log Cleared
description: The Windows Security audit log was cleared (event 1102) - a strong anti-forensics / defense-evasion signal that should almost never happen in normal operation.

name: Insider Threat: Successful Logon After Repeated Failures
description: Sequence of three or more failed logons (4625) followed by a successful logon (4624) for the same account within 10 minutes - a likely successful brute force.
query: sequence by user.name with maxspan=10m [any where event.code == "4625"] [any where event.code == "4625"] [any where event.code == "4625"] [any where event.code == "4624"]
